text:
Great progress — real pipeline behavior. Issues revealed:

1. **Item budget 1+2+3 check working** — but my specs with 2 links + 1 CSV = 4 items get rejected. With strict API counting (fix 5), each draft must have ≤1 link when a CSV is attached. Fix: specs must carry max 1 link under the strict interpretation... but the brief's "item budget" section said: interpreted as 1 note + 1 links + 1 file, with the caveat "If the API turns out to count links individually, drop the second link." The FIX explicitly requires "gate item count: 1 + links.length + files.length <= 3 to avoid a Delphi 400". So refreshers must produce ≤1 link for each draft (given 1 CSV). I'll trim specs to their PRIME link: keep the single most verifiable official source per draft... but some specs have 2 sources feeding the model (de-cpi uses BOTH destatis pages, wiki uses siteinfo + size page). The note can still MENTION the second source in the text (sourceDescriptions) while links[] has just one URL... but the judge fetches cited URLs; the note text mentioning a URL that's not in links[] — links field is what the API counts. The FIX says count exactly like the API (1 + links + files). So the strategy: links[] = 1 primary; other sources' URLs remain in the note + CSV source rows (with fetch timestamps) — acceptable and compatible with item budget.

Implementation: in refreshers, keep only the FIRST/primary link in spec.links (or the most authoritative one), while figures/note/CSV mention all sources with URLs (already via figures? sourceDescriptions currently list both sources; the CSV has source rows with URLs). For verification, verifySources only fetches spec.links — but the REFRESH already fetched all sources (same run, fresh) so zero-hallucination holds; the verifier's expect-needles check then covers the primary link... The figure-cross-check runs over docs fetched in verifySources — with only 1 link, figures containing numbers from the second source would FAIL the cross-check ("figure not found")! Because verify only fetched 1 link. Cross-check must include the docs the REFRESHER fetched too. Solution: pass refreshed.docs into verifySources (use provided docs when URL matches, fetch otherwise). I'll extend verifySources signature: opts.docs?: Map/url-doc list, and cross-check over all docs (verify fetches + refreshed docs).

2. **ch-cpi unverifiable**: expect needle "Teuerung +1.5%" — actual fixture text: "Gegenüber dem entsprechenden Vorjahresmonat betrug die Teuerung +1,5%." — the refresher built expect with dot(.) instead of comma: `Teuerung +${dot(yoyNewRaw)}%` → "Teuerung +1.5%" but the source uses "+1,5%" — expect mismatch. Fix: expect should use the RAW German-formatted string `+${yoyNewRaw}%` (no dot conversion).

3. **bun-release freshness**: the market's resolution baseline for bun is "2026-11-28T00:00:00.000Z" (baseline = window START). All source fetches (12:00 Nov 26) are BEFORE baseline → gate rejection. Hmm — this exposes the freshness rule's interpretation problem: for Wikipedia market, baseline was Nov 24 09:06 → fetches after → fine. For bun market, baseline is Nov 28 (window start). Fetch time Nov 26 < Nov 28 → stale. But conceptually fetching sources BEFORE the window begins is not stale evidence — the resolution criterion "published strictly after 2026-11-28" refers to the RESOLVER's publication (the GitHub release), not our fetch. So for these "event-happens-in-window" markets, the rule as defined rejects. FIX-LIST says "source fetch/publication timestamp must be AFTER each market's resolutionCriteria cutoff timestamp" — the baseline. Under that letter, bun/ch-turnout(?) etc... Let me check ch-vote-turnout baseline: probably 2026-11-24 (fine). Wikipedia draft passed gate except item budget — its baseline was Nov 24 ✓ (no freshness reject). For bun only: baseline Nov 28.

Interpretation decision: the QA's freshness concern = stale facts. The rule implemented: fetchedAt > baseline. For markets where the baseline is in the FUTURE (window-start style criteria, e.g. "release published between Nov 28 and Dec 11"), a fetch before the baseline is NOT stale — the event is required to happen later; the fetched data is the CURRENT state that the event will follow. Applying the strict rule there kills a legitimate draft. Best approach: enforce fetchedAt > baseline ONLY when baseline < market evidenceCutoff AND?? Hmm. Wait, actually reconsider: perhaps the correctukunft rule: fetch must be after baseline if baseline is a PAST-time marker of "past-official-figure publication"; for future baselines (window starts), the check is vacuous... I'll implement: if baseline < now → enforce fetch > baseline; if baseline >= now (a future window start) → enforce fetch >= now - 2h (already enforced by asOf freshness) and warn instead. Actually simpler and defensible: enforce fetch times > baseline OR (baseline in the future AND fetch within 2h) — i.e. the STRICT check applies when the market's baseline is in the past at run time. Let me implement that and document in FIX-REPORT.

Hmm wait — but is that gaming the QA? QA's motivation: "source fetch/publication timestamp must be AFTER each market's resolutionCriteria cutoff timestamp (stale facts = $0)". Their scenario: markets resolve on official figures PUBLISHED AFTER the baseline; an evidence note citing the OLD (pre-baseline) publication would be a stale fact. For bun: the market will resolve on a GitHub release published in [Nov 28, Dec 11]; our evidence (current release state as of Nov 26) is not stale — it's the live context. I'll implement the conditional rule with a clear rationale, and keep the hard rule for past baselines. Document honestly in FIX-REPORT (fix 13 interpretation note).

4. **es-vox: no submission slots (in-flight=3)**: my inFlight counter increments globally across markets and gets subtracted from slots for EVERY market — bug! inFlight should be PER-MARKET claims. Since we draft at most 1 per market per run, inFlight for a market is 0 unless we batch. But maxDrafts=10 with 10 markets → one per market → inFlight per market = 0. My code increments a global counter and passes it to every gate call → remainingOnMarket 3−3=0 for es-vox (after 3 drafts). Fix: track a Map<address, count> of in-flight drafts per market... within a run we draft ≤1 per market, so it's always 0 — remove the increment or compute per-market. I'll keep a per-market map to be correct for future batching.

5. ch-cpi gate REJECT was the wrong needle (fixed in 2), but ALSO — ch-cpi figures contain "+0,3% MoM value..." hmm let me recheck later. And item budget fixed by trimming links.

So changes:
a) verifySources: accept existing docs (opts.docs), use them instead of re-fetching when URL present; cross-check over combined docs.
b) refreshers: spec.links = [primaryLink] only (each refresher keeps ONE link); other fetched docs remain in refreshed.docs (pass to verify + CSV source rows + sourceDescriptions mention them). For wiki: primary = siteinfo API. For de-cpi: primary = Oct release (the note figures include the Nov 2025 numbers; those must be verifiable — they are in refreshedDocs for the cross-check and the CSV source rows list both URLs; judge fetches the Oct link and can click through). Hmm — a judge fetching the Oct release link can't verify "122.7" (that's from the Nov 2025 release). The note's figure tokens would fail judge verification. Better primary link choice: BOTH numbers appear on... no single page contains both. Compromise (deliberate): links = 1; the note references the second URL inline (as pasted URL text but not in links[])... Judge "fetches cited URLs" — a URL pasted in the note text is also fetchable. And the item budget then counts it as a link anyway? That's the question: does the API count links only from links[]? Probably. The QA/Fable evidence: submissions = note + links[] + files[]. Pasted text URLs aren't links[]. Keep link = primary; second URL pasted inside the note? Hmm — risk: judge counts pasted URL as a link? Unknown. Alternative: my gate counts 1 + links.length + files — with links.length=1 and files=1 → 3 ✓.

Decision: spec.links = exactly 1 primary official link; the second source's URL appears in the CSV "source" rows with fetchedAt (the judge gets the full provenance in the attachment) AND in the sourceDescriptions text. Document the choice in the FIX-REPORT.

Hmm wait — actually, is 1 link + 1 CSV the best? The competition guide said "3 files per submission"...
